title: What If Woolly Mammoths Walked the Earth Again?

scenes.text: What if woolly mammoths walked the Earth again? The DNA is the easy part.
Asian elephants share about 99.6 percent of their DNA with mammoths, so scientists are editing elephant cells.
The list of needed edits keeps growing, from about 65 genes at first to over 150 now.
Then comes the wait. An elephant pregnancy lasts about 22 months.
The first calf was promised for 2028. The company now says the early 2030s.
And it won't be a perfect copy. It would be a cold-resistant elephant with core mammoth traits.
